title: Split-Anisotropic Decomposition of a Torus
body_html:
Split-Anisotropic Decomposition of a Torus

Let \(T\) be a torus over \(k\). Then \(T\) contains

  • a unique maximal split subtorus \(T_d\), with \(X_*(T_d) = X_*(T)^{\Theta}\), equivalently with character lattice the maximal torsion-free quotient of \(X^*(T)_{\Theta}\); and
  • a unique maximal anisotropic subtorus \(T_a\), with \(X^*(T_a) = X^*(T)/X^*(T)^{\Theta}\);

and the multiplication map \[ T_d \times T_a \longrightarrow T \] is an isogeny: it is surjective with finite kernel, so \(T = T_d \cdot T_a\) with \(T_d \cap T_a\) finite. The decomposition is an almost direct product only: in general \(T \not\cong T_d \times T_a\).

Counterexample to directness. Let \(E/k\) be a separable quadratic extension and \(T = R_{E/k}\mathbb{G}_m\) (see Weil Restriction of Tori). Then \(T_d = \mathbb{G}_m\) (embedded diagonally), \(T_a\) is the norm-one torus Norm-One Torus of a Separable Extension, and \(T_d \cap T_a = \mu_2\). On character lattices, with \(\sigma\) the non-trivial element of \(\operatorname{Gal}(E/k)\) acting through the quadratic quotient: \(X^*(T) = \mathbb{Z}e_1 \oplus \mathbb{Z}e_2\) with \(\sigma\) swapping \(e_1, e_2\), while \(X^*(T_d \times T_a) = \mathbb{Z}(1) \oplus \mathbb{Z}(\mathrm{sgn})\). The swap module contains no basis of eigenvectors (its eigenvector sublattice \(\mathbb{Z}(e_1{+}e_2) \oplus \mathbb{Z}(e_1{-}e_2)\) has index \(2\)), so the two \(\Theta\)-lattices are not isomorphic and the tori are not isomorphic.
proof_html:
Write \(L = X^*(T)\).

Existence and shape of \(T_a\). The invariant sublattice \(L^{\Theta}\) is saturated in \(L\): if \(n\chi\) is \(\Theta\)-fixed with \(n \geq 1\) then \(n(\gamma\chi - \chi) = 0\), so \(\gamma \chi = \chi\) as \(L\) is torsion-free. By Subtori and Quotients via the Character Lattice the sublattice \(L^\Theta\) yields a subtorus \(T_a = H_{L^\Theta}\) with \(X^*(T_a) = L/L^{\Theta}\). It is anisotropic: \(\Theta\) acts through a finite quotient \(Q\), and the exact sequence \(0 \to L^Q \to L^Q \to (L/L^Q)^Q \to H^1(Q, L^Q)\) obtained from \(0 \to L^Q \to L \to L/L^Q \to 0\) begins with the identity map, while \(H^1(Q, L^Q) = \operatorname{Hom}(Q, L^Q) = 0\) because \(Q\) is finite and \(L^Q\) torsion-free; hence \((L/L^{Q})^{Q} = 0\). Any anisotropic subtorus \(S \subseteq T\) has character lattice a quotient \(L/L'\) with \((L/L')^\Theta = 0\); the image of \(L^{\Theta}\) in \(L/L'\) is fixed, hence zero, so \(L^{\Theta} \subseteq L'\) and \(S \subseteq T_a\): maximality.

Existence and shape of \(T_d\). A split subtorus corresponds to a saturated \(\Theta\)-stable \(L'\) with trivial action on \(L/L'\). The smallest such \(L'\) is the saturation of the augmentation sublattice generated by all \(\gamma\chi - \chi\), whose quotient is the maximal torsion-free quotient of the coinvariants \(L_{\Theta}\); the corresponding subtorus \(T_d\) is the maximal split subtorus, and dualizing the surjection \(L \twoheadrightarrow X^*(T_d)\) gives \(X_*(T_d) = X_*(T)^{\Theta}\).

Isogeny. The map on characters induced by multiplication is \[ L \longrightarrow X^*(T_d) \oplus X^*(T_a), \qquad \chi \longmapsto (\chi \bmod{}, \; \chi \bmod L^{\Theta}). \] Its kernel consists of \(\chi \in L^{\Theta}\) mapping to torsion in \(L_{\Theta}\); but for \(\chi\) fixed and non-zero the norm identification \(L^Q \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong L_Q \otimes \mathbb{Q}\) shows its image in \(L_\Theta \otimes \mathbb{Q}\) is non-zero, so the kernel vanishes. The two sides have equal rank (\(\operatorname{rk} L = \operatorname{rk} L^Q + \operatorname{rk} L/L^{Q}\) after tensoring with \(\mathbb{Q}\)), so the cokernel is finite. An injection of \(\Theta\)-lattices with finite cokernel corresponds to an isogeny of tori by F-Tori Are Classified by Galois Modules.
